methodology: Architectural review based on public documentation (station.jup.ag) and widely-documented JLP pool model. Program source is not publicly accessible at a standard GitHub repo.

evidence.architecturalNote: Jupiter Perps is a pool-based perpetual DEX. Traders open positions against the JLP (Jupiter Liquidity Provider) pool, not against other traders. There is no maker/taker matching step - every trade is user-vs-pool. This means the F7 'self-match bypassing haircut' attack surface does not exist here by construction.
evidence.lossModel: Trader losses flow to JLP holders collectively (pool absorbs). Trader wins drain the pool. There is no 'residual claim' surface that a winning trader can capture beyond their own position PnL.

findings.hasSocialisation: yes, but via pool drawdown distributed across ALL JLP holders
findings.socialisationNote: Because socialisation is across ALL LPs (every JLP holder), the F7 pattern 'I cause my own loss to absorb and claim my own residual' does not produce attacker gain - they would be diluting themselves alongside every other LP proportionally.
findings.confidence: high - structural, not dependent on specific code paths

notes: Pool-based perps (GMX-v1 style) are a different threat model from order-matched perps (Percolator, Drift). F7 is specific to order-matched designs with haircut residual accounting.
Jupiter Perps may have OTHER vulnerabilities specific to pool-absorption dynamics (e.g. oracle manipulation during large LP withdrawals) but they're not F7-class.
Closed-source program limits deeper audit. Architectural classification is defensible based on publicly documented model.
